surveys.name: Lake Survey chart of the Apostle Islands

places.name: The brownstone quarry, Stockton Island
places.text: Cut out and left when the market for brownstone failed: a spoil wharf, a derrick, and dressed blocks nobody came back for.

places.name: The Hermit Island quarry
places.text: The quarry company's cut on Hermit Island, idle since the Panic of '93. The men say they were never paid for the last month.

lines: The old quarry on Hermit Island's southwest shore has a wharf you can lie alongside in a calm. Nobody's worked it since '93.

places.name: The Basswood Island quarry
places.text: A brownstone cut on Basswood's west shore that sent stone to Chicago and Milwaukee, now worked only now and then.

places.name: The fish camp, Outer Island
places.text: Net reels, a shanty and a fish house on the sandspit at Outer Island's south end. Nobody fishes from it anymore.

places.name: The fish camp, Rocky Island
places.text: Herring fishermen's cabins and net sheds on the sandspit at Rocky Island's south end, where the tugs lie in the summer.

lines: The herring men keep a camp on Rocky Island's east side. They don't ask what a boat's carrying, so long as she buys their fish.

places.name: The fish camp, Manitou Island
places.text: A log cabin and a net shed above a stony beach on Manitou's southwest shore.

places.name: The farms at East Bay, Sand Island
places.text: A handful of Norwegian families farm and fish above East Bay, with a schoolhouse and a post office of their own.

places.name: The sea caves of Devils Island
places.text: The north end of Devils Island is honeycombed with caves the lake has cut into the sandstone. In a northeaster they boom like cannon.

lines: Go round the north end of Devils Island in a calm and you'll see caves in the cliff a man could row a boat into. In a blow you'll hear them first.

places.name: The sea caves at Swallow Point, Sand Island
places.text: Arches and caves along Sand Island's northeast shore, full of swallows in summer.

places.name: The mainland sea caves
places.text: A mile of red cliff on the mainland shore east of Siskiwit Bay, cut into caves and arches the lake runs right through.

lines: West of Sand Island the mainland's all red cliff, and the lake's gone right through it in places. Caves you could hide a boat in, if the sea let you.

places.name: Big Bay's sand spit and lagoon, Madeline Island
places.text: A long white beach across the mouth of a lagoon on Madeline's east side, with a bog and pines behind it.

places.name: Julian Bay, Stockton Island
places.text: Good holding in sand on Stockton's east side, open to the east but snug in a westerly.

lines: Caught out east of Stockton in a westerly, run into Julian Bay. Sand bottom, and the island takes the sea off you.

places.name: Quarry Bay, Stockton Island
places.text: The bay under the old quarry on Stockton's south shore: enough water off the spoil wharf, sheltered from the north.

places.name: Little Sand Bay
places.text: A small bay on the mainland across from Sand Island, shallow at the head, with a fisherman's dock.

places.name: Raspberry Bay
places.text: A wide bay on the mainland under Raspberry Island, out of a northwest sea.

places.name: Frog Bay
places.text: A quiet bay on the mainland east of Raspberry Bay, out of the way of the Bayfield traffic.

places.name: East Bay, Sand Island
places.text: The Sand Islanders' bay, with their dock at its head. Sheltered from the west.

places.name: Between Rocky and South Twin
places.text: The sound between Rocky and South Twin Islands, where the herring tugs lie in any weather but a southeaster.

places.name: Big Bay, Madeline Island
places.text: A broad bay on Madeline's east shore, open to the east and safe from everything else.

places.name: Sand Island Shoal
places.text: A reef of boulders between Sand and York Islands with two fathoms over it in places. Steamers give it a wide berth.

places.name: The shoals off Eagle Island
places.text: Rock all round Eagle Island, the furthest west of the Apostles, and the gulls' own.

places.name: Gull Island Shoal
places.text: A long reef running out northeast from Gull Island, past Michigan Island's light. The lake trout spawn on it; so do the wrecks.

lines: Steer well clear of Gull Island. The shoal runs out a mile and more to the northeast and there's next to nothing over it.

places.name: The bar off Chequamegon Point
places.text: Sand building out from the end of Long Island across the mouth of Chequamegon Bay. The range lights lead you round it.

places.name: The sandspit off Oak Island
places.text: A spit of sand reaching out from Oak Island's southwest point, barely awash in a low year.

places.name: The reef off Outer Island's north end
places.text: Rock under the light at Outer Island's north end. In fog the light is no help; the fog signal is.

places.name: The shoal off Bark Point
places.text: Rock off Bark Point at the mouth of Siskiwit Bay, not on any survey sheet: the logging tugs knew it.

legends.where: at the old light on Minnesota Point
in the caves of Devils Island
